title: Squad will sets the break-off line
overseerSummary: Approve with the negative-only seed both antagonists asked for: low morale or a spent squad leaves fights earlier; good housing never raises the death rate. The break-off log line prints the threshold.

proposals.title: One willingness axis: the squad's will sets the line for leaving a fight, and low morale seeds resolve
proposals.problem: temper.js:320 says the squad's bear line is where a temper is worth somebody's life, but that line is applied only between fights (field.js:362-381). A fight is resolved inside Combat.encounter, and the only way out of it is escapeHatch, which uses fixed constants (field.js:903-904, 1013), so a craven squad and a fearless one leave a losing fight at the same HP. Separately, morale and stamina never reach the field, and resolve (the existing -1..+1 'willingness to be here' that combat.js and broken() both read) starts at 0 for everyone and moves only on a death, so lodging, food, rest and bonds cannot change how a squad behaves in the dungeon. The party picker shows neither morale nor stamina (sortie.js:1033-1036). Measured on 1,500 combat-backed sorties per configuration, the line is worth deaths: squads in the most timid third die 0.616 per run against 0.682 for the boldest third, and low-morale squads die 0.664 against 0.622.
evidence: field.js:903-904 ESCAPE_HP 0.4, ESCAPE_LOW 0.2 and field.js:1013 `bad = (down > 0 && avg < 0.7) || avg < ESCAPE_HP || (lowest < ESCAPE_LOW && foeAvg > 0.4)`: no reference to willOf(s) or resolveOf(s) inside escapeHatch (field.js:989-1020).
field.js:362-381 broken() scales its lines by willOf(s).broken and `1 - 0.45 x resolveOf(s)`; temper.js will() builds broken.hp = clamp(0.25 x BEAR/bear(m), 0.06, 0.6).

field.js:571-591 grieved() is the only writer of a.resolve and adds to it, with an upward-only floor; sortie.js passes `a.fighter.resolve = a.resolve || 0` into combat.js before every fight; ACTOR_KEYS saves 'resolve'.

condition.js:133-153 moraleTarget already sums bed, food, rest, bonds, injury and temper into a 0-100 morale; its only consumers are moraleMult (town output) and the registry. condition.js:208-216 outcome(): +8 win, -12 loss, -6 per death.

Scratch real3.js (copy of the sortie loop, patched escapeHatch in a copy of field.js, morale drawn 60 +/- 22 per character and one in six members spent), 1,500 runs per configuration, same missions and squads. Terciles by Temper.will(party).broken.hp (bold = lowest line) and by mean morale. Baseline: deaths/run 0.635, win 47.6%; bold 0.682, mid 0.608, timid 0.616; morale low 0.664, mid 0.620, high 0.622.

Lean both ways (the earlier item 1, lean clamped 0.4-2.0): 0.615 deaths/run, win 47.9%; bold 0.774 (+13%), mid 0.596, timid 0.476. Lean raised only (clamp 1.0-2.0): 0.583, win 47.1%; bold 0.680, mid 0.592, timid 0.476. Raised-only lean plus negative-only seed: 0.561 (-12%), win 47.1%; bold 0.662, mid 0.566, timid 0.454; morale low 0.558 (-16%), mid 0.556, high 0.568. Both-way lean plus both-way seed (the earlier items 1 and 2): 0.609, bold 0.768, high morale 0.622 (no gain). Standard error about 0.03 on an aggregate and 0.05 on a tercile; seeds are paired by mission and squad.
sortie.js:1033-1036 the picker card shows stars, race, badge and scouting only; sortie.js:1018 omits injured characters.
proposals.change: 1) field.js escapeHatch: lean = clamp((willOf(s).broken.hp / BROKEN_HP) x (1 - 0.45 x resolveOf(s)), 1.0, 2.0), computed once when the hatch is built. The three lines become min(0.95, 0.7 x lean), min(0.75, ESCAPE_HP x lean) and min(0.45, ESCAPE_LOW x lean). The lean can only raise the lines, so a bold squad keeps today's constants and a timid or shaken one leaves earlier. The break-off log line prints the figure ('they break off the fight and run, below 52% average HP'), and Field.hatchLines(will, resolve) is exported so the picker prints the same number. 2) condition.js: resolveSeed(c) = clamp(min(0, (morale - 60) / 100) - (isSpent(c) ? 0.15 : 0), -0.4, 0). sortie.js launch sets a.resolve = resolveSeed(char) on each squad actor after F.start; the launch log lists each non-zero seed with the morale and stamina band that produced it. grieved() adds to the same variable and the floor is untouched. 3) sortie.js partyFacts (owned by systems-one-debrief): stamina and morale bands and caster pool percent on each card; the selected-party line adds Temper.readParty and 'leaves a fight below N% average HP, between fights below M%'.
proposals.playerEffect: Who goes together, and in what state, matters inside the fight. A rested, housed squad keeps today's lines. A squad whose last contract failed, or that went out twice without resting, starts with negative resolve and leaves earlier; a timid squad (low nerve and grit, or cunning) leaves earlier than today in every fight. Measured: deaths per run 0.635 to 0.561 (-12%), the timid third -26% (0.616 to 0.454), the low-morale third -16%, no third rises, win rate 47.6% to 47.1%. A bold squad is not changed, so boldness is a trade the player can still choose and the sheet shows the line.
proposals.secondOrder: Lodging morale (-18 to +22), bonds company (+/-14), the kitchen (+6 fed), injury (-15) and spent stamina from systems-one-debrief now reach permadeath through resolve. Grief floors and panic keep working because they write the same variable. combat.js:393-411 scales action values by resolve, so a shaken squad also covers itself more and attacks less; that effect is inside the measured numbers. Loop to watch: a lost contract (-12 morale) lowers the next seed, which makes the squad leave earlier, which can fail the next contract; it is bounded by the -0.4 floor (morale 20) and morale recovers about one point per resting tick, and the picker shows the band.
proposals.risks: Morale in the measurement is synthetic (60 +/- 22), not produced by the town simulation, so the spiral described above is not measured; the headless harness should run consecutive contracts with rest ticks between. A timid third leaves earlier and fails more contracts: its win rate went from 47.2% to 45.8% (n=500, inside noise). Lines above 0.5 make a squad leave while half its HP remains. The seed is read once at launch and persisted through ACTOR_KEYS 'resolve'. The positive side (high morale raises resolve) is deliberately not seeded: measured, it does not lower deaths and in the both-way lean it raises them for bold squads (+13%). Picker rendering is shared with other proposals; partyFacts is the single owner.
proposals.response: Design attack: item 2 now seeds from the negative side only (morale under 60 or spent), and item 1 only raises the lines, so good housing and food never raise the death rate. The requested bucket-style run is above: no tercile rises (bold 0.682 to 0.662, mid 0.608 to 0.566, timid 0.616 to 0.454; by morale 0.664/0.620/0.622 to 0.558/0.556/0.568) and the aggregate falls 12%. The earlier claim that the aggregate was flat came from the both-way version on the plain resolver; I reproduced its +13% for bold squads on the combat-backed driver (0.774) and removed the both-way behaviour. Items 1 and 3 are kept as asked; the picker shares an owner with loop-readout through partyFacts. Engineering attack: the seed is applied in the measurement (harness characters were given c.cond and a.resolve set at start), not only the escapeHatch patch; the lean is capped at 2.0 and shares one cap with any arcs change since it reads the same willOf and resolveOf; the picker shows the bands and the launch log prints each seed; the compounding after a failed contract is bounded and listed under risks as unmeasured.

verdicts.attack: Item 2 makes a well-housed, fed, rested squad stay in losing fights longer (bold tercile +12% deaths in the builder's own bucket run), so the town investments the game asks for raise the death rate under permadeath. The aggregate is flat (0.556 to 0.559 deaths/run), so it moves risk between squads rather than creating a decision the player can win. Item 1 is a one-line wiring of an existing axis into an existing mechanism and is the only part with a clear direction; item 3 is needed anyway by loop-wounds and systems-one-debrief.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: escapeHatch field.js:989-1020 uses fixed ESCAPE_HP/ESCAPE_LOW (903-904, 1013) with no willOf/resolveOf; broken() uses both (362-380); grieved() is the only writer of a.resolve (571-591); moraleTarget condition.js:133-153; combat.js:393-394 scales action values by resolve; sortie.js:1043-1045 shows no morale or stamina. sim/test/bucket.js is the stock harness with Temper.mood recorded per run; its aggregate 0.556 deaths/run matches my POW 0.45 run (0.54-0.55).
verdicts.demand: Keep item 1 (escapeHatch lines scaled by will and resolve, threshold printed in the break-off line) and item 3 (stamina and morale bands on picker cards). Seed resolve from the negative side only (morale under 60 or isSpent) so lodging and food never raise deaths; show one bucket run where no tercile's deaths/run rises. Picker rendering shares an owner with loop-readout.

verdicts.attack: Direction: positive resolve keeps a squad in a losing fight longer, and the builder's own tercile result (bold squads +12% deaths) means good housing and food raise the death rate for bold squads, against the permadeath priority. The seed also enters broken() through resolveOf (field.js:374-376), so the measured 10% (escapeHatch patch only) is partial. The seed is read once at launch, so a failed contract (-12 morale) compounds into the next launch.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified field.js:903-904 ESCAPE_HP/ESCAPE_LOW and the `bad` expression at 1013 with no willOf/resolveOf; broken() uses both at 362-380; grieved() (field.js:580-585) is the only writer of a.resolve apart from the floor clamp; sortie.js:167; combat.js:393-411 action values and fear line; condition.js:133-152 moraleTarget; picker cards show no morale or stamina (sortie.js:1043-1045). Bucket numbers not re-run.
verdicts.demand: 1) Seed only the negative side (morale below 60, isSpent) by default; a positive seed only if the user accepts the trade. 2) Scale escapeHatch by will as proposed but share one cap with loop-arcs. 3) Picker shows Condition.describe bands for stamina and morale and the launch log prints each seed. 4) Re-measure with the seed applied (harness characters need c.cond), not only the escapeHatch patch.
